tech.implementation:
Reconstruct the actual product's components as DOM (cards, numbers, chart states as SVG) using supplied brand tokens, fonts and copy. Neutral #F7F9FA/#263440 is used only for new presentation chrome. A GSAP timeline drives causal state changes: a button press, then a card expands as a shared element (FLIP measured once at build), then numbers count with tabular figures, then the chart path transitions. The camera is a wrapper transform with precise framing. Card labels carry data-reveal-after on their card container. X-ray recipe: exterior and interior supplied layers share one registered transform, and a feathered CSS mask-image radial position animated by GSAP replaces pointer input. No invented internals. 3s preview: tap 0–0.5s → card expansion 0.5–1.4s → metric/chart update 1.4–2.4s → hold. If no real product assets are supplied, report the gap instead of inventing a UI.
Optional recipe registered_xray: Register exterior/interior media with one coordinate system and shared transform. Reveal matching internal structure through a feathered mask without jumping scale or orientation; retain readable product labels. For export animate the mask with deterministic authored time instead of live pointer state. Keep the primary product/interface central; never manufacture unsupported internal features.
tech.render_pipeline:
Composition and export only: follow production_policy; integrate output from tech.style_renderer and tech.motion_engine.
Primary: HyperFrames. Author HTML/CSS/SVG compositions with data-composition-id, data-width, data-height, and data-duration. Time class="clip" elements with data-start and data-duration. Register one paused, seekable GSAP timeline per composition in window.__timelines[compositionId]; let the framework control media time. Run npx hyperframes check, inspect key moments with npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds>, and render with npx hyperframes render --quality delivery --output <video.mp4> under the task's authorization. Load local fonts and assets first, seed randomness, and drive Canvas/WebGL from shared time rather than wall clocks or independent loops.
Fallback: Remotion. Use this route only when HyperFrames is unavailable or cannot meet a required constraint, and document the checked limitation. Build React/Remotion compositions driven by useCurrentFrame and useVideoConfig, preload assets, seed randomness, and render through the Remotion CLI or @remotion/renderer in Node.js. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.
Delivery checks: inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames and watch the full video. Verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio synchronization, and loop continuity; fix issues and rerender.
tech.usage_note: These are suggested implementation routes, not claims about the source video's actual toolchain or locally installed tools. Tool combinations are selected as needed. Native Canvas and SVG do not require a 3D engine. Prepare assets and cache stateful simulations first; a simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples.

framework_selection.fallback_condition: Use Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable in the current environment or a verified limitation prevents a required capability or output. Record the specific reason. An existing React project alone is not a fallback reason.

Chartist and D3 are conditional alternatives if real data charts are required. Cropper and Sharp are unnecessary because CSS framing is non-destructive. Brand colors override the tokens completely.

The camera is a wrapper transform with precise framing. Card labels carry data-reveal-after on their card container. X-ray recipe: exterior and interior supplied layers share one registered transform, and a feathered CSS mask-image radial position animated by GSAP replaces pointer input. productionPolicy.principle: Select visual and motion technologies from the style, action, assets, and required fidelity before choosing the composition and export pipeline. Pipeline availability must not determine or simplify the visual style or motion technique.
productionPolicy.style_renderer: Owns visual construction: drawing, geometry, materials, lighting, typography, masks, textures, and specialist asset generation. Use the style-specific recommended technologies and implementation guidance.
productionPolicy.motion_engine: Owns trajectories, transforms, easing, transitions, deformation, and simulation. Select engines or algorithms appropriate to the action, with one owner for each animated property.
productionPolicy.render_pipeline: Owns scene assembly, composition timing, media and audio synchronization, validation, and final export. HyperFrames is the first choice; Remotion is the conditional fallback. Neither is the default visual construction or motion design method.
productionPolicy.integration: Visual and motion layers expose deterministic state at composition time, or supply baked assets or frame sequences. The pipeline supplies seekable time and composes their output. Timeline registration and frame hooks are integration adapters, not substitutes for style-specific rendering or motion.
productionPolicy.selection: Choose only needed stack entries. A technology may serve multiple roles, but document its actual responsibility. Optional authoring, interaction, color, and preprocessing tools are not mandatory renderers or motion engines.

motionReferences.name: Scroll-Driven Section Reveal and Card Stacking
motionReferences.description: Scroll reveals successive sections as overlapping cards. An earlier card stays at a defined anchor while the next rises over it; optional scaling or dimming makes the covered card recede. The active card stays readable and the stack eventually releases or exits as a group.
motion_sequence: Establish the first card and its sticky or pinned anchor.
Bring the next card over the anchored card; optionally reduce the covered card's scale or emphasis to communicate depth.
Repeat with a clear active-card hierarchy and readable holds, then release or exit the stack at a defined endpoint.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Schedule section progression on the video timeline. Calculate each card position and stacking state from time rather than intersection-event history. Give active content a reading hold and preserve a clear focal layer.

motionReferences.name: Radial Logo Burst

Keep tumbling confetti close around the icon; a strong sudden forward impulse toward the viewer slows into a very brief airborne hang, then a natural gravity-driven fall, never a canvas-wide distribution. Use an expanding circular mask for palette inversion while retaining the mark center. Let the burst decay into a stable logo hold; keep later particles subordinate. Use the icon center as the popper exit: pieces begin tiny at that point, shoot forward toward the viewer with a small spread around the center, never an upward launch, increase in apparent size, overlap in front of the icon, briefly hang and then fall. Keep the burst compact; express depth with coherent perspective scale and layer ordering.

motionReferences.name: Ranked Bar Race
motionReferences.description: Advance a time-indexed ranking: bar lengths and values change, rows travel to new ranks, and categories enter or leave the visible cutoff. Category labels and colors retain identity through every swap; the period indicator advances with the data.
motion_sequence: Establish the title, axis guide, ranked rows near their starting values, the period stamp and the source footer.
Advance the dataset: grow bars and update value labels from interpolated data.
When the order changes, slide rows to their new rank, keeping hue tied to category, and manage labels of crossing rows.
Fade rows in or out at the visible-rank threshold and step the period stamp at each data interval.
Slow or stop at the final period and hold the ranked result for reading.
motionReferences.video_adaptation: Precompute values, ranks and cutoff visibility for each category at each data step. Derive every frame from composition time, with a stable identity-to-color mapping, consistent value scale and coordinated period indicator. Keep labels attached to their categories and prevent unreadable collisions during swaps. Hold the final ranking for reading. Inspect units and cite the dataset; never invent factual values.

source_evidence.sampling: One actual source frame at each available integer second 01–08, individually reviewed by Claude Code Opus 5.5. Not continuous motion or audio analysis.

observations.observation: The bars start as slivers at the 2001 Q1 stamp and are longer at Q3. The leader changes (Iraq to Afghanistan), new rows enter, and each category keeps its hue and value-label color after changing rank.
Rows caught mid-swap overlap at 3s (Zimbabwe / Serbia and Montenegro / Iran) and at 7s (Turkey, with doubled value text). So rows slide to their new ranks rather than snapping.
In each sampled frame the bottom-threshold row is dimmed into the field (China, India, Czechia), and the large period stamp at bottom right steps forward by quarter.

limitations: The stills cannot show whether the bars grow continuously between quarters or in eased steps.
The stills do not show whether the axis rescales.
The collisions seen are a source flaw; the remedy suggested is adaptation, not observed.
Requires real, cited data; content and countries from the source must not be reused.

motionReferences.palette_guidance: Use a quiet, untextured field chosen for the topic and viewing context (dark or light). Give each category one distinguishable hue, checked for color-blind separation and for value-label contrast on that field. Use a neutral high-contrast ink for the title and period stamp, a muted neutral for axis, subtitle and source, and a fade toward field value for threshold rows.
